text:
Carmen: Hey team — pharmacy just rejected my specialty med (Solivex) at pickup. They say insurer denied for "step therapy - try formulary alternative first". I was on Solivex with my previous employer for a year, it works and I can’t switch. I started at Redwood 2026-06-01 and enrolled on day 1. Any ideas on next steps?
Priya (People Ops): Sorry you’re dealing with this. Two quick things: 1) confirm your plan effective date and bring any prior EOBs showing Solivex was covered; 2) ask pharmacy for an emergency/transition supply while we pursue an exception/prior auth. DM me the pharmacy name and date/time of denial and I’ll escalate.
OptiScript (Pharmacy): Hi Carmen 2211 we can do a 3-day emergency override if we get a provider attestation faxed to 555-0199. Denial message from carrier: code ST-05, suggested alternative: Formulix. PA ID required for further fills.
Carmen: Plan effective date shows as 2026-06-01. I have last employer EOBs that show Solivex paid through 2026-05-28 (gap of a few days during job transition). Provider can fax over notes. Really need this for weekend.
Liam (Benefits): Welcome Carmen. Step therapy requires trying the formulary alternative unless an exception is granted. For exceptions we need: clinical notes showing failure/intolerance to the step drug OR prior authorization/EOB showing Solivex coverage previously. Please have your provider submit a clinical justification and any prior EOBs. Email docs to benefits@redwood.com with subject: "RX exception request - Carmen - Solivex". For urgent/medical necessity cases we can request an expedited review (72 hrs).
Priya (People Ops): If you want, put me CC’d on the email and I’ll flag it as urgent. Also ask the pharmacy to give the 3-day transition fill now so you don’t run out.
PriorAuth Team: FYI we can submit a single-case exception to the medical director once we get the provider fax. Standard turnaround is 7-10 business days; expedited (life/limb/serious health risk) is 72 hours. Tracking if submitted: PA-99231 (pending).
Carmen: Provider faxed chart notes and last EOBs at 14:12. Pharmacy gave me a 3-day supply under emergency override so I have meds for the weekend. Thank you.
Liam (Benefits): Received docs. I’ve opened an expedited exception due to continuity of care during plan transition and attached the provider note + prior EOBs. We requested backdated coverage to 2026-06-01 while review is pending. Case: PA-99231. Expect decision in 24-72 hours given the expedited flag. If denied, next steps: administrative appeal (7-10 days) then external review/state appeal as needed.
benefits-bot: Solivex exception form & instructions: https://benefits.redwood.com/rx-exceptions. Required: provider clinical justification, prior EOB(s), medication history, NPI of prescriber. For urgent requests use subject: "URGENT: RX exception - patient name".
Carmen: Appreciate the fast move. Pharmacy said they’d hold future fills for 72 hrs. Any estimate on likelihood? I’m worried about a denial.
Liam (Benefits): We can’t promise an approval but continuity-of-care during recent plan transitions is a common grounds for exception, especially with prior paid EOBs. Medical director reviews clinical justification; if approved we can retro-authorize and the pharmacy will reprocess. If not approved, we escalate to appeals and can request single-case agreement pricing for a limited fill while appeal proceeds.
Priya (People Ops): Carmen, I’ll follow up with PriorAuth Team tomorrow and loop you in. If you get any EOBs or pharmacy receipts, forward to benefits@redwood.com and tag me. :thumbsup:
Carmen: Will do. Huge relief to have the 3-day supply. Thanks everyone!
PriorAuth Team: Update 24hrs later: exception approved by medical director, decision logged PA-99231-APPROVED. PriorAuth Team will notify pharmacy to reprocess with authorization for 90-day supply at retail specialty network. Pharmacy notification sent at 08:43.
Carmen: Got a call from OptiScript 2211 they reprocessed and my copay matched my old plan. Thank you all!!
